$comment: LIVE-1 / ADR-0165 — the CubeSandbox template contract for the live display.
This file is the machine-readable half of README.md and exists so the
template's promises can be CHECKED rather than read. scripts/
verify_display_attach.sh cross-reads it against the server's own constants
(subprotocol, capability prefix, endpoint grammar, host capability key), so
a template that drifts from the server it registers with fails a gate
instead of failing a person watching a black rectangle.
STATUS: runtime-unverified(cubesandbox webrtc producer). Nothing in this
repository can build or boot a CubeSandbox template, so every field below
is a DECLARED contract, proved at the contract level by
scripts/display_signaling_probe.py and not yet measured on a real microVM.
The unmeasured items are listed under `unverified` — they are part of the
spec, not a footnote to it.
ADR-0165 D1 names Selkies-GStreamer as the first preference with
`webrtcbin` as the alternative. This template declares the alternative,
and the reason is D4 rather than performance:
* ADR-0165 D4 requires view-only to be the ABSENCE of an input
datachannel, not a flag beside one. Selkies exists to deliver a
controllable desktop — its input datachannel is the product, and
view-only there is a configuration of a component built to provide
the thing we are refusing. `webrtcbin` has no input path at all
unless one is written, so the guarantee is the default rather than a
setting somebody can flip back.
* Selkies ships as a container image bundling an X session, a desktop
environment and a Python signalling server aimed at container/K8s
deployment; a CubeSandbox template is built from a rootfs.
This is a DECLARED choice on a structural argument, not a measured one —
see `unverified.producerSelection`. Swapping it is a one-field change
here plus the unit file; nothing in server-rust names a producer.

capture.$comment: The sandbox's own X display; the producer captures it and encodes.
capture.$audioComment: No audio track. A screen is what LIVE-1 shows; a microphone in a sandbox is a different consent conversation entirely.

producer.$inputComment: ADR-0165 D4, and still false: the producer MUST NOT add an application m-line to its OFFER. View-only remains the default shape of the connection, asserted by scripts/display_signaling_probe.py, which has a red proof (--prove-red) showing it catches a producer that does.

$comment: LIVE-3 / ADR-0004 증보 3. Control is now a grade the server can grant,
so the producer needs a way to open input — and exactly one way.
The trigger is the SERVER's answer, never the viewer's word. A producer
may negotiate an input datachannel if and only if its own
display-attach/validate call returned `input_enabled: true`, which the
server answers only when the bearer is a `controller` grant AND the
control window that grant opened is still standing (076). The viewer
asking is not authorisation and never becomes it — that is the same
principle as ADR-0165 D4's refusal to trust a client flag, applied one
grade over.
Because `input_enabled` is re-answered on every 30-second
re-validation, it is also the OFF switch: when the person hands control
back, the window closes and the next re-validation says false. The
producer MUST then close the datachannel rather than keep serving a
keyboard whose authorisation has lapsed. A returned window that leaves
a working keyboard is the failure this field exists to prevent.
Still runtime-unverified: no microVM was built or booted.

producer.$recordingComment: ADR-0165 D5. No frame is written to disk in the sandbox, and none reaches momo at all.

signalling.$subprotocolComment: The browser grammar: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: momo.display.v1, <capability>`, exactly as clients/web/src/features/work/observerStream.ts already dials a terminal with `momo.terminal.v1`. The producer echoes back the BARE subprotocol — echoing the capability would put a live bearer in every intermediary's response log.
signalling.$capabilityComment: One capability grammar for both kinds: 075 made the kind a column, not a second token format. See momo_t3::terminal_attach::CAPABILITY_PREFIX.
signalling.$endpointComment: `work_session_display_endpoint_ck` (075) accepts https and wss and refuses userinfo, query and fragment. A template publishes wss.
signalling.$revalidateComment: The producer re-validates on a timer for the life of the peer connection with `stream: true`, which relaxes expiry and ONLY expiry. That is what makes host revocation, observation=owner_only and a viewer leaving the channel cut a stream that is already open.

messages.$comment: `open_input` is in the viewer vocabulary and is refused with `{"type":"error","reason":"view_only"}` unless this producer's own validate answered `input_enabled: true` (see producer.inputDatachannelOnDemand). Accepting the word and deciding the act server-side is deliberate: a client that cannot even name the request cannot be told why it will not happen, and a client that names it still does not get to authorise it.

ice.$turnComment: ADR-0165 D3: no third-party TURN, ever. An oort-operated TURN is a separate decision that requires measuring whether direct connectivity works at all — see `unverified.iceReachability`. A `typ relay` candidate appearing in this path today means something is wrong, and the probe asserts its absence.
ice.$stunComment: Empty until the dedicated-host measurement says what is needed. Declaring a public STUN server here would be a third-party dependency introduced by default.

$comment: The ports the producer binds INSIDE the microVM. Whether and how they are
reachable from a browser on the internet is the open question of this
goal — see `unverified.iceReachability`. These numbers are declared so
that measurement has something concrete to test, not because the path is
known to work.

workdRegistration.$comment: How the sandbox's daemon tells momo it has a screen. Both calls are work-host-signed (Ed25519 v2 request signature); neither is reachable with a human bearer.

advertise.$comment: momo_t3::terminal_attach::HOST_DISPLAY_CAPABILITY_KEY. Issuance is fail-closed on this flag: a host that does not advertise has no screen, which is also how BYOC is excluded without policy naming a provider. 021's CHECK closes work_host.capabilities to booleans.

publishBinding.$comment: Publishing is once per session. Republishing the same pair is 204; a different pair is 409. The signer must be the session's own host — the path names a session, so that pin lives in the handler.

unverified.$comment: Named honestly rather than omitted (E5's lesson). Each entry is a claim this goal did NOT measure and must not be reported as working.
unverified.producerSelection: No CubeSandbox template was built or booted. `gstreamer-webrtcbin` is chosen on the ADR-0165 D4 structural argument above; whether it encodes acceptably inside a microVM with no GPU, and what the resulting latency is, is unmeasured.
unverified.iceReachability: Whether a browser can reach a producer inside a CubeSandbox microVM at all is UNMEASURED and structurally at risk. Two facts point at the risk: (1) nothing in the CubeSandbox adapter (server-rust/crates/momo-t3/src/provider/cubesandbox.rs) expresses inbound port exposure — `create_body` sends templateID, timeout, lifecycle, metadata and envVars, and no port map; (2) ADR-0157 증보 1 measured Cubelet's built-in eBPF `deny_out` blocking the sandbox's egress to every private range, which is a statement about the network posture these VMs ship with. If direct/host-reflexive ICE turns out not to work, ADR-0165 D3 says the answer is an oort-operated TURN and that is an ADR 증보, not a workaround this template may take.
unverified.templateBuild: The rootfs build (`--with-cube-ca=false` per ADR-0157 증보 1, the X server, the producer unit) is declared by this spec and the accompanying unit file, and has never been executed.
unverified.inputDelivery: LIVE-3 opened control on the SERVER: issuance, the control window, the non-observation gate and `input_enabled` are all exercised against a real PostgreSQL by display_attach_conformance_pg.rs. What is NOT measured is any of it reaching a screen — no producer has ever read `input_enabled: true`, opened a datachannel, delivered a keystroke to an X server, or closed that channel when the window was returned. The revoke half is the one to be most careful about reporting: it is a declared producer obligation here and a server statement in `validate`, and nothing in this repository can prove a producer honours it.
